title: Rest and play
hookLine: holy leisure is part of the rule
tomorrow: who walks in with you when you're the new kid somewhere?

lines: CAN A LAZY AFTERNOON BE HOLY?
THE FIRST WEEK ENDS WITH A DAY OFF.
cards: Two-a-days, a summer job, a phone that buzzes on vacation. Rest gets treated as what's left when the work runs out, and play as something you outgrow. So can a lazy afternoon be part of a holy life?
Ask the first page of the Bible. Its first week doesn't end with one last job. It ends with a day off.

teach.h: HE RESTED ON THE SEVENTH DAY.
teach.b: Genesis says God "rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done." Rest is built into creation, not earned after it.

teach.h: COME APART AND REST A LITTLE.
teach.b: When the apostles come back so busy they haven't had time to eat, Jesus says: "Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little."
Augustine had a name for it: holy leisure, the free time that love of truth goes looking for. And play?
The prophet Zechariah pictures a city healed, and here's the sign: "the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls, playing in the streets thereof."
One to tell a friend: in that prophecy, kids playing in the street is what a restored city looks like. Here's something Catholics share with their Jewish neighbors.
The Jewish Bible, in the JPS translation, says "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy," and Isaiah asks Israel to "call the sabbath a delight."
For Jews, Shabbat is a weekly gift, a delight and not a chore, and Catholics hear rest as a gift too.

And one honest difference: Jews keep the seventh day, Shabbat, with its own laws and customs; Catholics keep Sunday, the day of the resurrection, as the Lord's day, setting aside work that crowds out worship, joy and rest.
Two days, kept differently, and the same conviction: rest is holy.

how: Catholics keep Sunday as the Lord's day: Mass, and setting aside work that crowds out worship, family, works of mercy and rest. Some families keep a slow Sunday meal or an afternoon outdoors as part of it.

s: in the Bible, rest is a reward you earn once the work is finished
Genesis builds rest into the first week, and Jesus told busy apostles to rest a little.
Zechariah pictures a restored city full of boys and girls playing
playing in the streets thereof: that's what a healed city looks like.
Jews and Catholics keep the same day of rest
Jews keep Shabbat, the seventh day; Catholics keep Sunday, the day of the resurrection.

games.q: your family's Sundays have turned into errands and email after Mass. what change fits the Lord's day?
o: go to Mass, then use the rest of the day to get ahead on the week.
set aside the work that crowds out joy and rest, and keep a slow afternoon.
skip Mass when everyone's exhausted, since rest is the whole point.
games.why: Catholics keep Sunday with worship and with rest: setting aside work that crowds out joy, family and mercy. holy leisure is part of it.

practice: Sit back. Drop your shoulders, unclench your jaw and your hands, the way you would on a slow afternoon with nothing due. If a task shows up in your head, set it down for later.
When the time is up, put one block of rest on this week's calendar, and guard it like practice.

wordCard.voice: Rest and play. Time off that belongs in a holy life, from the first week of creation to kids playing in a healed city.

orig.note: Hebrew: sabbath, the day of rest in 'remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy'.

carryVoice: Your line: holy leisure. Rest is part of the rule, not a break from it. Go gently.
